msg: Self-declared age tick box. Ofcom lists self-declaration as not highly effective age assurance.
fix: Move the decision to an age-assurance provider or to the server; the visitor must not be able to answer for themselves.

msg: Date of birth typed by the visitor is the gate. A typed birth date is self-declaration wearing a form.
fix: Drop the field, or pass it to a provider that estimates or verifies rather than believes it.

msg: The pass is kept in browser storage, so the gate opens for anyone who edits one key.
clause: OSA 2023 s.12 — access must be effective, not advisory
fix: Keep the decision on the server and give the browser a signed, short-lived token.

msg: The age pass lasts months or years, so the check never repeats for a shared or resold device.
fix: Shorten the pass to a session or a small number of days and re-run the check after that.

msg: The restricted page is already in the DOM and a class toggle uncovers it — view-source walks past the gate.
fix: Do not send the restricted markup until the server has seen a pass.

msg: A card is used as proof of age. Ofcom excludes payment methods that are available to under-18s.
fix: Only a card type restricted to over-18s counts; otherwise use a listed age-assurance method.

msg: A warning sentence stands in for a gate. A disclaimer is not age assurance.
fix: Keep the sentence, but put a real check behind it.

msg: This page gates on its own. No listed age-assurance method (photo-ID match, facial age estimation, open banking, mobile-network check) appears anywhere in the file.
clause: Ofcom HEAA guidance, section 3 — the listed methods
fix: Hand the decision to one of the listed methods and keep the response server-side.
